items.quote: Classification including 5 µm particles may be considered where indicated by the CCS or historical trends.

items.statement: For grade D, the manufacturer establishes in operation particle limits based on a risk assessment and, where applicable, routine data.
items.quote: The manufacturer should establish in operation limits based on a risk assessment and routine data where applicable.

items.quote: and all critical processing areas, such as the point of fill and container closure feeder bowls, should be evaluated.

items.statement: Determine critical processing locations by a documented risk assessment and knowledge of the process and operations carried out in the area.
items.quote: Critical processing locations should be determined by documented risk assessment and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.statement: Carry out cleanroom classification in both the at rest and the in operation states.
items.quote: Cleanroom classification should be carried out in the at rest and in operation states.

items.statement: Achieve the at rest total particle limits of Table 1 after a clean-up period following completion of operations and line clearance or cleaning.
items.quote: The total particle limits given in Table.1 above for the at rest state should be achieved after a clean-up period upon completion of operations and line clearance or cleaning activities.
items.condition: after operations and line clearance or cleaning

items.statement: Determine the clean-up period (guidance value under 20 minutes) during room qualification, document it, and follow it in procedures to restore a qualified state of cleanliness if disrupted during operation.
items.quote: The clean‑up period (guidance value of less than 20 minutes) should be determined during the qualification of the rooms, documented, and adhered to in procedures to reinstate a qualified state of cleanliness if disrupted during operation.
items.condition: if cleanliness is disrupted during operation

items.statement: Clearly justify the air speed of unidirectional airflow systems in the qualification protocol, including where air speed is measured.
items.quote: The speed of air supplied by unidirectional airflow systems should be clearly justified in the qualification protocol, including the location for air speed measurement.

items.statement: Design, measure and maintain air speed so that unidirectional air movement protects product and open components at the working position, e.g. where high-risk operations occur and product or components are exposed.
items.quote: Air speed should be designed, measured and maintained to ensure that appropriate unidirectional air movement provides protection of the product and open components at the working position (for example, where high-risk operations occur and where product or components are exposed).

items.statement: Unidirectional airflow systems provide a homogeneous air speed of 0.36–0.54 m/s (guidance value) at working level, unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.
items.quote: Unidirectional airflow systems should provide a homogeneous air speed in a range of 0.36–0.54 metres per second (m/s) (guidance value) at the working level, unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.
items.condition: unless scientifically justified in the CCS

items.statement: Airflow visualization studies correlate with the air speed measurements.
items.quote: Airflow visualization studies should correlate with the air speed measurement.

items.statement: Determine the microbial contamination level of cleanrooms as part of cleanroom qualification.
items.quote: The microbial contamination level of the cleanrooms should be determined as part of the cleanroom qualification.

items.statement: Base the number of microbial sampling locations on a documented risk assessment, room classification results, air visualization studies and process knowledge.
items.quote: The number of sampling locations should be based on a documented risk assessment and the results obtained from room classification, air visualization studies, and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.quote: Qualification should include both at rest and operational states.

items.statement: Grade B microbial limits during qualification: air sample 10 CFU/m³, settle plates (90 mm) 5 CFU/4 hours, contact plates (55 mm) 5 CFU/plate.
Grade C microbial limits during qualification: air sample 100 CFU/m³, settle plates (90 mm) 50 CFU/4 hours, contact plates (55 mm) 25 CFU/plate.
Grade D microbial limits during qualification: air sample 200 CFU/m³, settle plates (90 mm) 100 CFU/4 hours, contact plates (55 mm) 50 CFU/plate.
Expose settle plates for the duration of operations, changing them as required or after no more than 4 hours.
items.quote: Settle plates should be exposed for the duration of operations and changed as required, or after a maximum of 4 hours.

items.statement: Base settle plate exposure time on recovery studies.
items.quote: Exposure time should be based on recovery studies

items.statement: Settle plate exposure time does not allow the media to dry out.
items.quote: and should not allow desiccation of the media used.

items.statement: Use all methods listed for a grade in Table 2 when qualifying an area of that grade.
items.quote: All methods indicated for a specific grade in the table should be used for qualifying the area of that specific grade.

items.statement: If a listed method is not used, or alternative methods are used, justify the approach appropriately.
items.quote: If one of the methods tabulated is not used, or alternative methods are used, the approach taken should be appropriately justified.
items.condition: if a listed method is not used or alternatives are used

items.statement: If technologies reporting results other than as CFU are used, scientifically justify the limits applied and, where possible, correlate them to CFU.
items.quote: If different or new technologies are used that present results in a manner different from CFU, the manufacturer should scientifically justify the limits applied and where possible correlate them to CFU.
items.condition: if technologies not reporting CFU are used

items.statement: For qualification of personnel gowning, apply the contact plate and glove print limits of Table 6.
items.quote: For the qualification of personnel gowning, the limits given for contact plates and glove prints in Table.6 should apply.

items.statement: Sampling methods do not create a contamination risk to manufacturing operations.
items.quote: Sampling methods should not pose a risk of contamination to the manufacturing operations.

items.statement: Requalify cleanrooms and clean air equipment periodically following defined procedures.
items.quote: The requalification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment should be carried out periodically following defined procedures.

items.statement: Requalification includes at minimum: cleanroom classification (total particles), final filter integrity test, airflow volume measurement, verification of pressure differences between rooms, and air velocity test.
items.quote: The requalification should include, at a minimum, the following: i. cleanroom classification (total particle concentration); ii. integrity test of final filters; iii. airflow volume measurement; iv. verification of air pressure difference between rooms; v. air velocity test.

items.statement: For grades B, C and D, perform the air velocity test according to a risk assessment documented in the CCS.
items.quote: For grade B, C and D, the air velocity test should be performed according to a risk assessment documented as part of the CCS.

items.statement: The air velocity test is performed for filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow, e.g. filling of terminally sterilized products or background to grade A and RABS.
items.quote: It is however, required for filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow (for example, when filling terminally sterilized products or background to grade A and RABS).

items.statement: For grades with non-unidirectional airflow, perform a recovery test instead of velocity testing.
items.quote: For grades with non-unidirectional airflow, a recovery test should replace velocity testing.

items.statement: Requalify grade A and B areas at intervals of no more than 6 months.
items.quote: The maximum time interval for requalification of grade A and B areas is 6 months.

items.statement: Requalify grade C and D areas at intervals of no more than 12 months.
items.quote: The maximum time interval for requalification of grade C and D areas is 12 months.

items.statement: Carry out appropriate requalification, including at least the listed tests, after remedial action for an out of compliance equipment or facility condition, or after changes to equipment, facility or processes, as appropriate.
items.quote: Appropriate requalification consisting of at least the above tests should also be carried out following completion of remedial action implemented to rectify an out of compliance equipment or facility condition or after changes to equipment, facility or processes, as appropriate.
items.condition: after remedial action or changes to equipment, facility or processes

items.statement: Determine through the change management process whether a change is significant enough to require requalification.
items.quote: The significance of a change requiring requalification should be determined through the change management process.

items.statement: Clean and disinfect cleanrooms thoroughly according to a written programme.
items.quote: They should be cleaned and disinfected thoroughly in accordance with a written programme.

items.statement: Clean to remove surface contamination before disinfecting.
items.quote: For disinfection to be effective, cleaning to remove surface contamination should be performed prior to disinfection.

items.statement: Cleaning programmes effectively remove disinfectant residues.
items.quote: Cleaning programmes should effectively remove disinfectant residues.

items.statement: Use more than one type of disinfecting agent so that, where modes of action differ, their combined use is effective against bacteria and fungi.
items.quote: More than one type of disinfecting agent should be employed to ensure that where they have different modes of action, their combined usage is effective against bacteria and fungi.

items.statement: Disinfection includes periodic use of a sporicidal agent.
items.quote: Disinfection should include the periodic use of a sporicidal agent.

items.statement: Monitor regularly to assess the effectiveness of the disinfection programme and detect changes in microbial flora types, e.g. organisms resistant to the current regime.
items.quote: Monitoring should be undertaken regularly in order to assess the effectiveness of the disinfection programme and to detect changes in types of microbial flora (for example, organisms resistant to the disinfection regime currently in use).

items.statement: Validate the disinfection process.
items.quote: The disinfection process should be validated.

items.statement: Disinfection validation studies show disinfectants are suitable and effective as actually used, on the surface material type (or justified representative material), and support in-use expiry periods of prepared solutions.
items.quote: Validation studies should demonstrate the suitability and effectiveness of disinfectants in the specific manner in which they are used and on the type of surface material, or representative material if justified, and should support the in-use expiry periods of prepared solutions.

items.statement: Disinfectants and detergents used in grade A and B areas are sterile.
items.quote: Disinfectants and detergents used in grade A and B areas should be sterile.

items.statement: Disinfectants used in grade C and D areas may need to be sterile where the CCS determines this.
items.quote: Disinfectants used in grade C and D areas may also be required to be sterile where determined in the CCS.

items.statement: Where the sterile product manufacturer dilutes or prepares disinfectants and detergents, do so in a way that prevents contamination and monitor them for microbial contamination.
items.quote: Where the disinfectants and detergents are diluted or prepared by the sterile product manufacturer, this should be done in a manner to prevent contamination, and they should be monitored for microbial contamination.
items.condition: where diluted or prepared by the manufacturer

items.statement: Apply appropriate procedures during production to verify, monitor and record FFS critical process parameters and equipment operation.
items.quote: The appropriate procedures for the verification, monitoring and recording of FFS critical process parameters and equipment operation should be applied during production.

items.statement: Operational procedures describe how forming and sealing issues are detected and corrected.
items.quote: Operational procedures should describe how forming and sealing issues are detected and rectified.

items.statement: Record and investigate rejected units and sealing issues.
items.quote: Rejected units or sealing issues should be recorded and investigated.

items.statement: Establish risk-based maintenance procedures that include maintenance and inspection plans for tooling critical to unit sealing effectiveness.
items.quote: The appropriate maintenance procedures should be established based on risk, and should include maintenance and inspection plans for tooling critical to the effectiveness of unit sealing.

items.statement: Document and investigate any identified issue that indicates a potential product quality concern.
items.quote: Any issues identified that indicate a potential product quality concern should be documented and investigated.

items.statement: Install BFS equipment used for terminally sterilized products in at least a grade D environment.
items.quote: BFS equipment used for the manufacture of products that are terminally sterilized should be installed in at least a grade D environment.

items.statement: Conditions at the BFS point of fill comply with the environmental requirements of paragraphs 8.3 and 8.4.
items.quote: The conditions at the point of fill should comply with the environmental requirements of paragraphs 8.3 and 8.4.

items.statement: For shuttle-type aseptic BFS, areas of parison extrusion, blow moulding and sealing meet grade A conditions at the critical zones.
items.quote: Therefore the areas where parison extrusion, blow moulding and sealing take place should meet grade A conditions at the critical zones.

items.statement: For shuttle-type aseptic BFS, design and maintain the filling environment to meet grade A viable and total particle limits at rest and in operation.
items.quote: The filling environment should be designed and maintained to meet grade A conditions for viable and total particle limits both at rest and when in operation.

items.statement: For rotary-type aseptic BFS, design and maintain the filling environment within the parison to meet grade A viable and total particle limits at rest and in operation.
items.quote: The filling environment within the parison should be designed and maintained to meet grade A conditions for viable and total particle limits both at rest and when in operation.

items.statement: Install aseptic BFS equipment in at least a grade C environment, provided grade A/B clothing is worn.
items.quote: The equipment should be installed in at least a grade C environment, provided that grade A/B clothing is used.
items.condition: provided grade A/B clothing is used

items.statement: Perform microbiological monitoring of operators wearing grade A/B clothing in a grade C area according to risk management principles.
items.quote: The microbiological monitoring of operators wearing grade A/B clothing in a grade C area should be performed in accordance with risk management principles.
items.condition: operators in grade A/B clothing in grade C
